text: THE MASTHEAD NO LONGER MOVES THE PAGE WHEN IT CONDENSES, AND THE WEBSITE'S PHONE MASTHEAD RUNS THE GESTURE. The header is in flow, so condensing took its lost height out of the DOCUMENT — measured on the website home at 89px on desktop and 135px on a phone, with the scroll position dragged after it: a flick of 900px landed at 765. `SiteHeader` now remembers its resting height and gives the difference back as `--sa-hdr-reserve` while condensed, so the document's height never changes and nothing under the header moves. Below `breakpoint/tablet` the website masthead also takes the portals' gesture: scrolling down carries the condensed bar away, any upward flick brings it back with the accessibility bar, and the UX4G floating button is hidden at every scroll position (accessibility-entry-point.md rule 4b, extended from the layered portals). That button had been sitting on the assistant's launcher — 285,718 against 275,696 at 375px wide — which is why the assistant read as missing.
